/itineraryStops/3/highlights/2.source_en: 1.5 m wide; capacity ~900 adults; designed for 30 m/s winds and magnitude-7 earthquakes

/itineraryStops/3/highlights/3.source_en: 10 m above ground — family-safe, kid-friendly wobble; 10-15 min stair climb from parking

/itineraryStops/3/highlights/4.source_en: Strongest in late October to early November autumn foliage (red maple + golden oak frame the red bridge)

/itineraryStops/3/highlights/5.source_en: **Officially opened March 2018**, fundraised by Paju Mayor Lee In-jae's citizen-donation campaign under the slogan 'Freedom is not free — it is earned with blood'

/itineraryStops/3/highlights/6.source_en: **1.7 km from Gloucester Hill Battle Memorial** (the actual April 22-25 1951 battlefield) — guests choosing the full Gloucester Memorial visit add 30-45 minutes to the route

/itineraryStops/3/highlights/7.source_en: **Bridge specs**: spans Seolmari Valley severed by Highway 37 — Korea's longest pier-less suspension bridge per Korea Tourism Organization official designation

/itineraryStops/3/highlights/8.source_en: **Open daily 09:00-18:00**; bridge crossing FREE; **parking ₩2,000 (credit card only)** at Lot 1 (closest to bridge entrance — recommended for elderly guests)

/itineraryStops/3/smartNotes/tip.source_en: The bridge wobble is strongest in the middle — children love it; visitors with vertigo should grip the railings and walk slowly. Avoid in heavy wind (occasional closures). Early morning has the best light and lowest crowds; mid-afternoon weekend visits in October can be very busy.

/itineraryStops/3/smartNotes/facilities.source_en: Small cafe + snack stalls at the parking area; minimal facilities at the bridge itself. CU convenience store within ~5 min drive for a more substantial snack stop.

/itineraryStops/3/whyOnRoute.source_en: Ending the day on Gamaksan turns the route into more than a memorial-only experience — the red-bridge-against-forest visual contrasts strongly with the morning's underground tunnel and barbed-wire DMZ horizons, giving the day a lighter, photo-friendly close that travelers consistently rate as the trip highlight. It is also a deliberate Korean War tribute — the Gloucester Regiment dedication ties the afternoon thematically back to the morning's DMZ history without imposing more heaviness on the mood.

/itineraryStops/3/convenience/parking.source_en: 2,000 KRW (credit card only at most lots; foreign cards generally accepted). Park at Lot 1 — closest to bridge — to save significant walking.

/itineraryStops/3/description.source_en:
After lunch, the route shifts from heavy history to mountain scenery. The Gamaksan Chulleong Bridge — officially named 'Gloucester Heroes Bridge' in honor of the 1st Battalion of the British Army's Gloucester Regiment, who fought heroically against superior Chinese forces at the Battle of the Imjin River in April 1951 — is a striking red suspension bridge spanning the Seolmari Valley on Gamaksan Mountain (675 m, one of the closest peaks to the DMZ). 

Per Visit Korea (gov't authoritative), the bridge is 150 meters long; some operator sources cite 220 m, but that figure most likely conflates this bridge with the nearby Majangho Suspension Bridge across Majang Lake (also in Paju, also 220 m). Confirm with your driver-guide which bridge the day visits. 

The bridge is approximately 10 m above ground (low enough to be family-safe; high enough to feel the wobble), 1.5 m wide, with capacity for ~900 adults simultaneously, and engineered to withstand 30 m/s sustained winds and magnitude-7 earthquakes. 

From Parking Lot 1 (closest to the bridge), a stair climb of about 10-15 minutes reaches the bridge entrance; the bridge itself is a flat crossing of the valley. Late October through early November autumn foliage is the iconic season; spring green and summer canopy views are also strong. 

The bridge is named for the **British 1st Battalion Gloucester Regiment** (the 'Glorious Glosters'), which on April 22-25, 1951, with the 170th Mortar Battery, held the strategic ridge above the Imjin River for four days against three Chinese PLA divisions, allowing the broader UN line to retreat south of Seoul. 

Of 622 Glosters who entered the battle, only 39 returned to UN lines — the rest were killed, wounded, or taken prisoner. Paju City under Mayor Lee In-jae raised construction funds via citizen donation campaign in 2017-2018, dedicating the bridge under the slogan **'Freedom is not free — it is earned with blood.'**

/itineraryStops/3/visitBasics/hours.source_en: Bridge 09:00-18:00 daily; hiking trails sunrise to sunset

/itineraryStops/3/visitBasics/closed.source_en: Open year-round (occasional closures for high winds)

/itineraryStops/3/visitBasics/walking.source_en: Moderate — 10-15 min stair climb from parking; bridge itself is a flat 150 m crossing
